title: Hankyung: five South Korean savings banks, now including Hana, hit by hacking since late September
date_note: Hankyung's article of 24 November is the only source; the individual intrusions are not dated here beyond the article's own wording.
org: South Korean savings banks (Hana, OK, Welcome, DB, Yegaram)
geo_basis: country named in the source; no city given, pin at Seoul
summary: Hankyung reports that five savings banks (Yegaram, Welcome, DB, OK and Hana) have been hit by hacking since late September, according to its exclusive tally. For Hana, the article says an intrusion into its mobile customer identity re-verification system exposed identity-verification data including names, resident registration numbers, phone numbers and addresses. A Hana official told the paper the bank has blocked the external IP addresses involved and is monitoring around the clock.
plain: Hankyung reports five South Korean savings banks have been hacked since late September. Hana Savings Bank says it has blocked the IP addresses involved and is monitoring around the clock.
exec: Hankyung's tally of five hacked savings banks shows customer identity data at smaller Korean lenders is being exposed through web-linked services.

validation.note: Only Hankyung's article of 24 November was read; none of the banks' own notices were read, and the individual intrusion dates were not checked.
